title: The Impact of Having a Tattoo on Fertility Treatment Outcome
official: The Impact of Having a Tattoo on Fertility Treatment Outcome: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: Tattoos are increasingly common among women of reproductive age, yet their potential systemic inflammatory effects and impact on fertility treatment outcomes are unknown. This prospective observational cohort study aims to evaluate whether the presence, size, duration, and ink characteristics of tattoos are associated with pregnancy outcomes following embryo transfer in women undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Women aged 21-40 years Undergoing IVF with planned fresh or frozen blastocyst embryo transfer Availability of good-quality blastocyst embryos Willingness to provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

Significant untreated uterine abnormalities

≥3 prior failed embryo transfers Hydrosalpinx in situ BMI \>40 kg/m² Age \>41 years at embryo creation Submucosal fibroids in situ Use of medications affecting implantation (e.g., chronic steroids, metformin)
sponsor: McGill University Health Centre/Research Institute of the McGill University Health Centre
